faq.heading: Common Questions
faq.intro: Straight answers to what homeowners and facility managers ask us most. Don't see yours? Call or send the form and we'll walk you through it.

items.question: How long does a garage floor take?
items.answer: Most two- and three-car garages are ground, repaired, coated, and flaked in a single day. You can walk on the floor the next morning, move light items back in after 24 hours, and park on it after 48 hours. Larger shops and commercial floors are scheduled in phases so you can keep working.

items.question: What's the difference between epoxy and polyaspartic?
items.answer: Epoxy is a thick, strong base coat that bonds to the concrete and builds the floor. Polyaspartic is a faster-curing, UV-stable topcoat that won't yellow in sunlight and resists hot-tire pickup and chemicals. We use epoxy where it belongs, on the base, and polyaspartic on top, which is why our floors go in fast and hold up outdoors.

items.question: How do you prep the concrete?
items.answer: Every floor is diamond-ground with dust-collecting grinders to open the pores of the concrete so the coating bonds mechanically. We then fill cracks and spalls, grind them flush, check for moisture, and vacuum everything before the first coat goes down. Acid etching and paint rollers from a big-box kit skip this step, which is why those floors peel.

items.question: Will it peel or hot-tire lift like the kit I tried?
items.answer: No. Peeling comes from poor prep and thin, water-based coatings. We grind the slab, use 100% solids epoxy for the base, and finish with a polyaspartic topcoat that stays put under hot tires, dropped tools, and oil. Our residential floors carry a 15-year warranty against peeling and delamination.

items.question: Can you coat old, cracked, or stained concrete?
items.answer: Almost always. Cracks and chips are repaired and ground flush before coating, and a full-flake floor hides stains and surface imperfections completely. During the free estimate we test for moisture and check for structural problems; if a slab needs a moisture-mitigation primer or isn't a good candidate, we'll tell you up front.

items.question: Is it slippery when wet?
items.answer: A full-flake floor has natural texture from the chips, and we can add an anti-slip additive to the topcoat for patios, pool decks, entryways, and shop bays where water or oil is expected. Glossy marble floors can be finished satin or with a light grit for the same reason.

items.question: How do I clean and maintain it?
items.answer: Sweep or dust-mop as needed and hose it off or mop with warm water and a little neutral cleaner. There's no waxing or sealing to keep up with. Avoid rubber-backed mats sitting in one spot for months and use a dolly instead of dragging heavy steel edges across the floor.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: Pricing depends on square footage, the condition of the concrete, and the system you choose, so we quote every floor after a free on-site measurement. A typical two-car garage flake floor is priced by the square foot, and bigger shops and commercial floors get volume pricing. There's never a charge for the estimate.

items.question: Do you work on commercial and industrial floors?
items.answer: Yes. We install high-build epoxy, urethane mortar, and quartz systems for warehouses, shops, restaurant kitchens, gyms, clinics, and retail spaces, including line striping, safety zones, cove base, and drains. Night and weekend installs are available so you don't lose production time.

items.question: Are you licensed and insured?
items.answer: We're a veteran owned and operated company, fully insured, and every crew member on your property works directly for us. Ask and we'll gladly send a certificate of insurance before the job starts.

full-flake.title: Epoxy Flake Floors
full-flake.intro: Vinyl color chips broadcast into a 100% solids epoxy base and locked under a UV-stable polyaspartic topcoat. It's the floor we install more than any other, because it looks good on day one and still looks good ten years later.

sections.heading: Where Epoxy Flake Floors Can Be Used
body: Flake works anywhere concrete takes abuse and needs to stay clean. The texture hides dust and tire marks, and the topcoat shrugs off water, sun, and chemicals, so the same system covers a two-car garage, a covered patio, and a 10,000 sq ft shop.
bullets: Residential garages and carports
Workshops, barns, and metal buildings
Patios, porches, walkways, and pool decks
Basements, laundry rooms, and mudrooms
Auto shops, detail bays, and showrooms
Retail floors, gyms, vet clinics, and locker rooms
Warehouses, storage rooms, and light manufacturing

sections.heading: Why Choose Epoxy Flakes
body: A flake floor isn't paint. It's a bonded, seamless coating system that becomes part of the slab. Compared with bare concrete, tile, or a roll-on kit, it holds up better and costs less over its life.
bullets: Hot-tire resistant: the polyaspartic topcoat won't lift or peel under a warm tire
Hides dirt, dust, and stains between cleanings
UV stable, so outdoor and sun-facing floors don't yellow or chalk
Seals porous concrete against oil, salt, and moisture stains
Installed in one day on most garages, back in use within 48 hours
30+ color blends to match trim, cabinets, or brand colors
Backed by our 15-year residential warranty against peeling

sections.heading: The Installation Process
body: Every floor gets the same prep whether it's 400 square feet or 40,000. Most of the work, and most of the difference between a floor that lasts and one that peels, is in the first two steps.

steps.title: Estimate & moisture test
steps.text: We measure the space, check the slab for moisture and existing coatings, and pick a blend and finish with you.

steps.title: Diamond grinding
steps.text: Industrial grinders with dust extraction open the pores of the concrete so the epoxy bonds mechanically. No acid etching.

steps.title: Crack & spall repair
steps.text: Cracks, chips, and joints are filled with a fast-cure repair mortar and ground flush.

steps.title: Base coat
steps.text: A pigmented 100% solids epoxy or polyaspartic base coat is rolled on and back-rolled for even build.

steps.title: Flake broadcast
steps.text: Vinyl chips are broadcast into the wet base coat to full refusal, so no base color shows through.

steps.title: Scrape & vacuum
steps.text: Once cured, loose chips are scraped off and vacuumed, leaving a uniform, lightly textured surface.

steps.title: Clear topcoat
steps.text: A UV-stable polyaspartic clear coat locks the chips in and adds the gloss, chemical resistance, and optional anti-slip grit.

steps.title: Cure & walk-through
steps.text: Walk on it the next morning, move light items back after 24 hours, and park after 48. We walk the floor with you before we leave.

sections.heading: Safety Features
body: Flake floors are used in commercial kitchens, hospitals, and fire stations for a reason: they're easier to keep safe than the concrete they cover.
bullets: Built-in texture from the chips gives more grip than smooth concrete or tile
Optional anti-slip aggregate in the topcoat for wet areas, pool decks, and entries
Seamless surface with no grout lines, cracks, or edges to trip on
Light-colored blends brighten garages and shops and improve visibility
Chemical resistant, so spilled oil, gas, brake fluid, and cleaners wipe up instead of soaking in
Low-odor polyaspartic topcoats let you back in the space the same day
Cove base and drain detailing available where floors need to be washed down

sections.heading: Maintaining Your Epoxy Floor
body: There's no sealing, waxing, or refinishing schedule. A little routine care keeps a flake floor looking new for years.
bullets: Sweep or dust-mop as needed; rinse with a hose or mop with warm water and a neutral cleaner
Wipe up oil, gas, and chemical spills when you see them
Skip harsh solvents, citrus strippers, and abrasive pads
Put a pad under jack stands, kickstands, and sharp steel edges
Lift heavy equipment instead of dragging it across the floor
If a section ever dulls after years of hard use, a fresh clear coat brings it back without redoing the floor
